tagline: Grab a bag of peas. It's going to be a big night.
about: A hard-drinking country rock star walks into a drag bar, hears a young singer and pulls her into the spotlight.

tbsp olive oil1 lemon, zested and juiced1 bunch mint, leaves picked1 tsp salt and pepper, to taste8 slices of sourdough1 clove of garlic, halved200g fresh ricotta1/2 tsp dried chilli flakes30g parmesan, shavedCook the peas in boiling salted water for 3 minutes and drain.Smash roughly with 2 tbsp of the oil, the lemon zest and juice, most of the mint and salt and pepper.Toast the sourdough, rub with the cut garlic and drizzle with the rest of the oil.Spread with ricotta, pile on the peas and finish with chilli flakes, parmesan and the rest of the mint.Lorenzo's kitchen table aranciniCrumbed fried risotto balls with parmesan and peas around a mozzarella centre, with warm tomato sauceHow to make it1 small brown onion, finely chopped30g butter300g arborio rice1 L hot vegetable stock50g parmesan, finely grated1/2 cup frozen peas125g mozzarella, in 16 cubes50g plain flour2 eggs, beaten100g dried breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying400g passata4 basil leaves1/2 tsp saltSoften the onion in the butter, stir in the rice, then add the stock a ladle at a time until thick and creamy.Stir in the parmesan and peas, spread on a tray and chill until firm.Roll into 16 balls around a cube of mozzarella, roll in flour, dip in egg and coat in breadcrumbs.Deep-fry at 180°C in batches until deep golden, and drain.Warm the passata with the salt and basil and serve with the arancini.MainsLorenzo's limo crew meatballs and spaghettiPork and beef meatballs with parmesan and parsley in a slow tomato, garlic and basil sauce, over spaghetti with more parmesanHow to make it500g beef and pork mince2 tbsp olive oil1 brown onion, finely chopped4 cloves of garlic, 1 grated for the meatballs, 3 sliced for the sauce2 x 700g bottles of passata1 bunch basil1 tsp dried chilli flakes2 tsp salt500g spaghetti60g parmesan, finely grated1 egg60g fresh breadcrumbs60ml milk1/2 bunch flat-leaf parsley, choppedSoak the breadcrumbs in the milk, then mix with the mince, egg, grated garlic, half the parmesan, parsley and 1 tsp of the salt. Roll into 16 balls.Bake on an oiled tray at 200°C for 15 minutes.Meanwhile soften the onion and sliced garlic in the oil, add the passata, chilli, basil stalks and the rest of the salt and simmer 20 minutes.Slip the meatballs into the sauce and simmer gently.Cook the spaghetti, drain and toss with some of the sauce, then serve with the meatballs, torn basil and the rest of the parmesan.SweetsCatering shift cannoliCrisp cannoli shells filled with sweetened vanilla and orange ricotta, ends dipped in pistachios and dark chocolate, dusted with icing sugarHow to make it500g firm ricotta100g icing sugar, plus extra for dusting1 tsp vanilla extract1 orange, zested50g dark chocolate, finely chopped12 cannoli shells40g pistachios, choppedDrain the ricotta in a sieve in the fridge.Beat with 80g of the icing sugar, the vanilla and orange zest until smooth, then fold in the chocolate.Spoon into a piping bag and chill.Pipe into the shells from both ends, dip the ends in pistachios and dust with the rest of the icing sugar.DrinksDrag night cosmopolitanVodka, orange liqueur, cranberry and fresh lime shaken hard and served straight up with an orange twistHow to make it160ml vodka60ml orange liqueur240ml cranberry juice3 limes, juiced1 orange, peel only, for twists2 cups iceChill 4 coupe or martini glasses.Shake the vodka, orange liqueur, cranberry juice and lime juice hard with the ice.Strain into the glasses and twist an orange peel over the top.Gin martini with a twistJack's order, poured strong at the end of the bar.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
